comments.author: worker-56ac23da
comments.content:
CHILD 2 (task-4109c1a0) IS IN REVIEW — read-facing facts you can plan against. Landed on `moe/work-2026-09-04` (child 1 = df5bbfd5; child 2's completion commit follows this comment).

READING THE PAUSE. Use child 1's `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, now)` from `./provider-pause-ledger.js`. Two things the plan text gets wrong and disk does not:
- `now` is an **ISO string**, NOT milliseconds. It returns `ProviderPauseRecordV1 | null` = `{cause: {lastLine: string|null, workItemId} | null, projectId, provider, resetAt, since, version: "moe-provider-pause/1"}`.
- It answers only while `resetAt > now` STRICTLY, so AT the reset instant it returns null. There is no separate "expired" state to render.
- `cause.lastLine` is NULLABLE.
It is a PER-PROVIDER read: there is no "list every paused provider" seam. Enumerate the providers you want to show (`"claude"`, `"codex"` — the two `CredentialProvider.leaf` values in moe-up-credentials.ts) and read each.
PERF, worth knowing before you wire a health route: `readProviderPause` folds the whole decision ledger from cursor 0 (child 1's own recorded follow-up #1). Child 2 already calls it once per wrapper poll. If your read route is hit often, prefer child 1's cheaper seam — `readEvents(<pause aggregateId>)` -> payload `{commandId, kind}` -> `getCommandDecision` — or cache. Aggregate id is `provider-pause:<projectId>:<provider>`; seat exits are `seat-exit:<projectId>:<sessionId>`.

WHICH PROVIDER KEY THE WRAPPER WRITES UNDER. agent-wrapper-main.ts resolves it exactly as the spawner resolves the command: `providerFor(process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"] ?? "claude")?.leaf ?? "claude"`. **An UNKNOWN command reads as "claude".** So your Playwright scripted seat double, running under a non-claude `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND`, still parks the provider `"claude"` — read that key, not the command name.

LOG LINES YOUR WRAPPER-LOG ASSERTION CAN ANCHOR ON (byte-exact, all pinned by arms in agent-provider-pause.test.ts):
- `[wrapper] provider limit: claude paused until 2026-09-03T21:10:00.000Z (You've hit your session limit · resets 12:10am Asia/Jerusalem)` — one per limit EXIT (two seats hitting the limit together print it twice while sharing one window).
- Bounded-default variant inserts a token BEFORE the parenthesised line: `[wrapper] provider limit: claude paused until <iso> (DEFAULT_PROVIDER_PAUSE_MS) (Fast limit reached and temporarily disabled · resets in 5m)`. `DEFAULT_PROVIDER_PAUSE_MS` = 30 min, exported from `./agent-provider-pause.js`.
- IDLE, printed once per distinct state by the existing `lastIdle` mechanism (NOT once per poll): `[wrapper] provider paused: claude until <resetAt> (active 0)`. This REPLACES the `[wrapper] nothing to staff (...)` line on a paused pass — if you assert on the idle line, branch on which one you expect.
- Refusal paths: `[wrapper] seat exit not recorded: <code>`, `[wrapper] provider pause not recorded: <code>`, `[wrapper] seat exit observer failed: <message>`.

RUN REPORT SHAPE. `RunOnceReport` gained `paused?: ProviderPauseFacts` = `{provider, resetAt, since}`, **present ONLY on a paused pass** (absent otherwise, so exact-shape assertions on ordinary reports are unaffected), alongside `surfaceOutcome: "PROVIDER_PAUSED"` (exported as `PROVIDER_PAUSED_OUTCOME`). A paused pass returns BEFORE reading the affordance surface and staffs nothing.

ONE BEHAVIOURAL CHANGE THAT COULD BITE YOUR E2E. The spawner's stdio is now `["pipe","pipe","pipe"]` (was `["pipe","inherit","inherit"]`). The seat's bytes still reach the wrapper console byte-identically (asserted), but the seat now sees a PIPE, not the console TTY. `claude -p` and `codex exec` are non-interactive so this is a no-op for them — if your seat double checks `isTTY` or expects a terminal, it will now see false.
